provenance.lineage_summary: GPDF frozen D0/D1 variant contracts retained; independent Python rational algorithm with explicit numerical corrections. Dev9 successor of exact document SHA256 ee0d984e3ed4852af703810b460819bc02881901d1210eb15cf83b60be3779cd; unchanged contracts are reused, changed numerical methods and failure closure follow GPDF-R1/R2/R3.
provenance.license_status: Private development only; source numerical data redistribution grant NOT_ESTABLISHED; NumPy and SciPy notices retained.
public_references: Weideman (1994), Computation of the Complex Error Function, doi:10.1137/0731077
Xie (2013), Generalized Plasma Dispersion Function, arXiv:1305.6476

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for nonfinite/empty phase points, invalid integer order or unsupported pole count.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Fixed approximation has no iterative convergence claim.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result after a failed call.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: FloatingPointError if continued result exceeds finite float64 range.

scope: Default and explicit order, scalar/matrix shapes, reflection, normalization, positive imaginary axis overflow regression.
80-digit mpmath equation grid and 70-digit independent Gaussian Cauchy integrals.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Validated finite grid and identities, not a uniform error certificate across the complex plane.
known_limitations: Fixed truncation error depends on phase point and order.

summary: Faddeeva 32 阶变体；保留独立默认值、截断及失败合同。

identity.definition: Weideman rational FFT expansion with erfcx on imaginary axis.
identity.boundary: Real axis is accepted; exponential continuation overflow raises.

supported: Finite nonempty scalar or array input; shape preserved.
preconditions: All phase values and computed results fit complex128.

inputs.name: order
inputs.description: Rational truncation or pole count. None selects order 32.
inputs.constraints: Any positive integer order. Boolean rejected.

example.code:
from scirel.kinetic import evaluate_faddeeva_gpdf
import numpy as np
r=evaluate_faddeeva_gpdf(0.2+0.7j)
assert np.isfinite(r["w"])
example.expected: Finite complex response with the retained effective order.
